name: Cannabis and the 2018 Farm Bill
where_it_stands: The 2018 Farm Bill legalized hemp by defining it as cannabis with no more than 0.3% delta-9 THC, which opened the door to intoxicating hemp products. Congress replaced that definition in November 2025 with a total-THC standard due to take full effect on 11 December 2026, while the House-passed 2026 farm bill awaits Senate action.

next_milestone.text: New hemp definition takes full effect, closing the 2018 Farm Bill's delta-9 'loophole' unless Congress acts.

summary: The Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (Pub. L. 115-334), signed on 20 December 2018, removed hemp from the Controlled Substances Act and set up USDA-approved state, tribal and federal hemp production plans. Because the definition counted only delta-9 THC, courts such as the Ninth Circuit read it to cover hemp-derived delta-8 and other cannabinoids, fueling a national market for intoxicating hemp. Public Law 119-37 rewrote the definition in November 2025. The House passed a new farm bill, H.R. 7567, on 30 April 2026 by 224-200; it adds industrial hemp provisions but does not delay or repeal the hemp THC ban, and Hemp Law Group reports the Senate committee version also leaves the ban untouched.

what_changes.text: Hemp growers for fiber and grain keep federal protection, and the House bill would ease testing for designated industrial hemp; cannabinoid product makers face the new limits.
The farm bill is not the vehicle the hemp THC industry hoped for; further relief would need separate legislation.
Products sold under the 2018 Farm Bill's delta-9 reading lose federal cover when the new definition applies.

timeline.event: 2018 Farm Bill becomes law, legalizing hemp at 0.3% delta-9 THC
USDA publishes its final domestic hemp production rule
Ninth Circuit holds hemp-derived delta-8 THC products fit the Farm Bill's hemp definition
Public Law 119-37 rewrites the federal hemp definition
House passes the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 (H.R. 7567), 224-200
New hemp definition takes full effect after a 30-day delay

faq.q: Did the 2018 Farm Bill legalize THC?
faq.a: It legalized hemp, defined as cannabis with no more than 0.3% delta-9 THC. Courts read that to cover other hemp-derived THC forms, which Congress has now moved to close.

faq.q: Does the 2026 farm bill change the hemp THC ban?
faq.a: The House-passed bill does not delay or repeal it; it focuses on industrial hemp production and testing.

faq.q: Is there a new farm bill yet?
faq.a: No. The House passed H.R. 7567 in April 2026; it has not been enacted.
